q: Chlorine has proton number 17. Which statement about chlorine is correct?
options: Its electronic configuration is 2,8,7 and it is in Group VII
Its electronic configuration is 2,8,7 and it is in Group III
Its electronic configuration is 2,7,8 and it is in Group VII
Its electronic configuration is 2,8,7 and it is in Period 7
explain: 17 electrons give 2,8,7. Seven outer electrons means Group VII, and three occupied shells means Period 3.

q: Which statement about the carbon atom in a molecule of CO₂ is correct?
options: It shares two pairs of electrons and has two non-bonding pairs
It shares four pairs of electrons and has no non-bonding pairs
It shares four pairs of electrons and has two non-bonding pairs
It shares two pairs of electrons and has no non-bonding pairs
explain: Carbon forms two double bonds, so it shares 4 pairs, using all of its 4 outer electrons; no non-bonding pairs remain.

q: Which electronic configuration belongs to a noble gas?
explain: 2,8,8 is argon, with a full outer shell. The others have incomplete outer shells.

q: What is the formula of potassium bromide?
options: K₂Br
KBr₂
KBr
K₂Br₂
explain: Potassium forms K⁺ and bromine forms Br⁻; equal charges mean one of each ion.

q: Which row correctly describes the electrical conductivity of the two forms of carbon?
options: conducts | conducts
does not conduct | does not conduct
conducts | does not conduct
does not conduct | conducts
explain: All the outer electrons in diamond are used in bonding; graphite has delocalised electrons between its layers.

q: How many non-bonding pairs of electrons are in the outer shell of nitrogen in ammonia, NH₃?
explain: Nitrogen has 5 outer electrons: 3 are shared with hydrogens and the other 2 form one non-bonding pair.

q: Which formula is correct for lithium oxide, made of Li⁺ and O²⁻ ions?
options: Li₂O
LiO
LiO₂
Li₂O₂
explain: Two Li⁺ ions (+2) balance one O²⁻ ion (−2).

q: Which row correctly gives the numbers of particles in the ion ³⁹₁₉K⁺?
explain: Protons = 19, neutrons = 39 − 19 = 20, and the 1+ charge means one electron fewer than the protons: 18.

q: Which particle contains 18 electrons?
options: K⁺ (proton number 19)
Na⁺ (proton number 11)
Cl (proton number 17)
Ca (proton number 20)
explain: K⁺ has 19 − 1 = 18 electrons. Na⁺ has 10, a chlorine atom has 17 and a calcium atom has 20.

q: The symbol ¹⁴₇N represents an atom. Which statement is correct?
options: The atom has 7 protons and 7 neutrons
The atom has 14 protons and 7 neutrons
The atom has 7 protons and 14 neutrons
The atom has 7 protons and 21 neutrons
explain: The lower number is the proton number (7). Neutrons = 14 − 7 = 7.

q: Which statement about the proton number (atomic number) is correct?
options: It is the number of protons and neutrons in an atom
It is the number of neutrons in an atom
It is the number of protons in the nucleus of an atom
It is the number of outer shell electrons
explain: Proton number is defined as the number of protons in the nucleus, and it identifies the element.

q: An oxygen atom (2,6) forms an ion. What is the ion?
options: O⁶⁻
O²⁺
O⁺
O²⁻
explain: Oxygen gains two electrons to complete its outer shell, giving 2,8 and a charge of 2−.

q: Which pair of atoms are isotopes of each other?
options: ¹⁴₆C and ¹⁴₇N
¹²₆C and ¹⁴₆C
¹²₆C and ¹²₅B
¹⁶₈O and ¹⁴₆C
explain: Both carbon atoms have 6 protons but different mass numbers (12 and 14), so they differ in neutron number only.

q: What is the mass number (nucleon number) of an atom?
options: The number of protons only
The total number of protons and neutrons in its nucleus
The total number of protons and electrons
The number of neutrons only
explain: Mass number counts the particles in the nucleus: protons plus neutrons.

q: How many protons and neutrons are in an atom of ¹²₆C (the number 12 is the mass number, 6 is the proton number)?
options: 6 protons and 12 neutrons
12 protons and 6 neutrons
12 protons and 12 neutrons
6 protons and 6 neutrons
explain: Protons = 6; neutrons = 12 − 6 = 6.

q: Which is the best description of metallic bonding?
options: The attraction between oppositely charged ions in a lattice
The sharing of pairs of electrons between atoms
The electrostatic attraction between positive ions in a lattice and a sea of delocalised electrons
The weak attraction between neutral atoms
explain: A metal is a giant lattice of positive ions surrounded by delocalised electrons that are free to move.

q: How many pairs of electrons are shared in a molecule of methane, CH₄?
explain: Carbon forms four single bonds, one with each hydrogen atom, so four pairs are shared.

q: Why are metals malleable?
options: Layers of positive ions can slide over each other while the electrons keep them bonded
Their atoms are held in separate molecules
Their ions repel each other when forced
The bonds between atoms break and re-form with the same partners
explain: The sea of electrons holds the ions together even when layers move, so the metal changes shape without breaking.

q: How many covalent bonds are in one molecule of water, H₂O?
explain: The oxygen atom shares one pair of electrons with each of the two hydrogen atoms.

q: Which substance has a structure most similar to silicon(IV) oxide?
options: Graphite
Diamond
Sodium chloride
Methane
explain: Both diamond and SiO₂ are giant covalent structures in which each atom is bonded to four others.

q: Which sample of sodium chloride conducts electricity?
options: Solid sodium chloride
A pressed pellet of solid sodium chloride
Dry crystals of sodium chloride
Molten sodium chloride
explain: Ions are free to move only when the compound is molten or dissolved in water; they are fixed in position in the solid.

q: Why is diamond used in cutting tools?
options: It is soft and easily shaped
It conducts electricity well
It has layers that slide
It is very hard because of its strong covalent bonds in all directions
explain: Each carbon atom is held by four strong covalent bonds in a rigid structure, making diamond extremely hard.

q: Diamond has a very high melting point. What is the reason?
options: Many strong covalent bonds must be broken to melt it
Weak forces between molecules must be overcome
Strong ionic attractions must be overcome
The bonds between layers are very strong
explain: Diamond is a giant covalent structure, so melting requires breaking large numbers of strong covalent bonds.

q: Magnesium has three isotopes: ²⁴Mg (79%), ²⁵Mg (10%) and ²⁶Mg (11%). What is its relative atomic mass, to one decimal place?
A particle has 17 protons and 18 electrons. Which is correct?
options: It is a neutral atom
It is a positive ion with a charge of 1+
It is a negative ion with a charge of 1−
It is a negative ion with a charge of 2−
explain: One more electron than protons gives a net charge of −1, so the particle is an anion (Cl⁻).

q: Which particles are found in the nucleus of an atom?
options: Protons and neutrons
Protons and electrons
Neutrons and electrons
Electrons only
explain: The nucleus contains protons and neutrons; electrons are found in shells outside the nucleus.

q: Which statement about the components of a mixture is correct?
options: They are joined by chemical bonds in a fixed ratio
They always lose their own properties
They can only be separated by a chemical reaction
They keep their own properties and can be separated by physical methods
explain: The parts of a mixture are not chemically combined, so each keeps its own properties and can be separated by physical methods such as filtration or distillation.

q: Why do metals conduct electricity?
options: Delocalised electrons are free to move through the lattice
Positive ions are free to move through the lattice
Metals contain negative ions
Metals contain molecules that carry charge
explain: Metal ions are fixed in the lattice, but the delocalised electrons carry charge when a voltage is applied.

q: Why is graphite used as a lubricant?
options: Its layers can slide over each other easily
It has very strong covalent bonds between layers
It is a good insulator
It has a very low melting point
explain: The forces between layers are weak, so the layers slide past each other.

q: What is the electronic configuration of a chloride ion, Cl⁻ (chlorine has proton number 17)?
explain: The chlorine atom (2,8,7) gains one electron, giving 18 electrons arranged 2,8,8.
